subject: T423: multi-model whole-Bible chunking fork (experimental)
summary: Logos-scripture-graph is trying a speed fork: 4-5 AI models each run a continuous whole-Bible chunking marathon in separate scratch folders (M1_cursor..M5_composer_alt), starting from the same research baseline (literature types, grammar, Strong's G/H, wj/red-letter, observation substrate). After marathons: agreement spans = easy/consensus chunks; disagreement delta = governed focus queue. If fork fails, revert to T410 parallel_chunking_research_program baseline. Red-team pre-mortem required before marathons.

subject: Request: independent red-team pre-mortem of T423 fork
summary: Before any whole-Bible marathon starts, an independent AI should run .ai/prompts/multi_model_whole_bible_chunking_redteam_premortem_prompt.md and write .ai/scratch/multi_model_bible_chunking/redteam/REDTEAM_PREMORTEM_REPORT.md with GO/HOLD/ABANDON_FORK verdict.

subject: T441 lesson candidate: Rust no-text coverage index after parser contracts
summary: A useful pattern for high-resource evidence work is: Python no-text fixture or pilot, then source-specific parser contract with negative fixtures, then a narrow Rust leaf tool that scans/counts/hashes and emits no-text JSON/JSONL coverage ledgers, with Python remaining the authority validator. Count parity is coverage evidence only, not semantic authority. A file named index must distinguish generated coverage/index ledgers from retrieval or vector indexes.

lesson_candidate.pattern: no-text fixture -> parser contract -> Rust no-text coverage leaf tool -> Python authority validator
lesson_candidate.use_when: Large deterministic source-observation coverage or parity scans would otherwise be slow or error-prone in Python or by AI rereading.
lesson_candidate.avoid_when: Governance interpretation, theology decisions, preferred readings, alignment truth, translation judgments, or production evidence-root promotion are being decided.
